newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian protests spread in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian protests spread in West Bank.

text.p: Israeli-Palestinian clashes spread on Wednesday to the West Bank town of Ramallah where hundreds of rock-throwing Arabs charged an Israeli army roadblock, drawing volleys of teargas and rubber bullets.

Hospital officials in self-ruled Ramallah said 25 Palestinians were treated for rubber bullet wounds or teargas inhalation on the seventh day of violent protests in the West Bank over Israeli settlement policy in Arab East Jerusalem.
In Bethlehem, Palestinians clapped and whistled as they burned Israeli and American flags.
U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross prepared to return to the region for crisis talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Hundreds of Arabs swept past Palestinian police and hurled rocks towards Israel's Araq checkpoint outside Ramallah as other protesters threw stones on the main highway linking the town to Jerusalem, just to the south.
Israeli rushed reinforcements to the scene as troops repulsed the challenge with rubber bullets and teargas.
It was the first time in the current wave of violence that clashes which have been limited mainly to Bethlehem and Hebron, also in the West Bank, have erupted in Ramallah.
Palestinians have said Israel's settlement drive strengthens its hold in East Jerusalem, which Palestinians claim as the capital of their future state.
Israel, which captured East Jerusalem along with the rest of the West Bank in the 1967 Middle East war, sees all of Jerusalem as its capital.

The PLO has brought the matter to the United Nations where the United States twice vetoed decisions condemning the Israeli plan. The American flag burned in Bethlehem had the word "veto" scrawled on it.

The U.S. State Department said it was sending its chief Middle East peace broker to the region to try and defuse the tensions. A Palestinian official said Ross would meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Morocco this week.

An Israeli security source said troops had orders to show restraint in dealing with Palestinian demonstrations and try to avoid casualties. Last September, 61 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed in gunbattles during Palestinian protests against Israel's policy in Jerusalem.
"The troops are trying not to fire at Palestinian police so as not to provoke them to fire back," the source said.
Palestinian security chief in the West Bank, Jibril Rajoub, was in Bethlehem on Wednesday trying to keep the Palestinian protest from getting out of hand.
On Friday, an Islamic militant blew himself up in a Tel Aviv cafe, killing three women and triggering an Israeli security alert around major cities.
